newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PORT ELIZABETH AIRPORT READY FOR 747S IN 1998.
newsitem.headline: PORT ELIZABETH AIRPORT READY FOR 747S IN 1998.

text.p: Port Elizabeth's airport will achieve international capacity by late 1998 following an upgrade and runway extension programme.

Kevin Wakeford, chief executive of the Port Elizabeth Chamber of Commerce, said the upgrade -- which will cater for 747s -- would be a major boon to local flower growers and sea food suppliers, as well as helping the tourist industry.
"It means we will be able to overnight roses and marine products and top quality engineering products to international markets," he said.
The Port Elizabeth area boasts some of southern Africa's largest rose growing nurseries while the fishing industry produces a rich catch of oysters, mussels and other shellfish.
Tourism is also growing and Wakeford said he expected charter operators to take advantage of the international capacity once the extension is completed in 18 months time.
The airport currently handles some 50 domestic passenger flights a day to and from Johannesburg, Cape town, Durban, Bloemfontein, East London, George, Plettenberg Bay and Umtata.
In addition, South African Airways operates five freighters per night to Johannesburg and Cape Town.
